absent: Interrupt budgeting policy, numeric interrupt ceiling, and sampling predicate details.
Auxiliary capture, BPF consumption rules, overflow handler registration, and address allowance checks.
Trap work execution, poll and async wakeup semantics, and user page update contents.
Recursion context management, register snapshot pool use, and PMU stop ordering.
Hash width and bucket count, online mask maintenance, and allocator behavior.
Tracepoint lifecycle, filter predicate language, BPF array validity, and trace call layout.
Static key and jump entry layouts, architecture patch primitives, module linkage, and boot state treatment.
Full locking and memory ordering between overflow, scheduling, and event release paths.

findings.text: Hardware overflow entry requires disabled interrupts and forwards to a shared overflow routine with throttling requested, returning that routine outcome. The shared routine discards non sampling work, budgets interrupts, suspends auxiliary capture around handling, gives attached perf BPF logic first chance to consume the sample, then handles countdown limit, trap notification, registered callback and deferred async wakeup.

Overflow countdown starts from a sampled limit value. When the limit is nonzero and reaches zero on decrement, the event becomes disabled, asks its PMU to stop, and records hangup; otherwise it records input readiness. Deferred wakeup is queued only when asynchronous interest exists together with a recorded readiness state.

Trap handling derives a pending identity from the sampled instruction address, selects NMI safe versus resume notification from current context, and coalesces to a single outstanding work item while protecting against fast context switch and holding a reference. Repeated trap capable overflows with kernel excluded warn on identity mismatch, treating address change as forward progress.
Each CPU holds a software hash control with a pointer to bucket storage plus a mutex plus a reference count. Buckets are indexed by a hash and hold RCU protected event lists.

Period setup refreshes the last period from the configured sample period and atomically deducts whole periods from remaining credit, reporting how many periods elapsed and reporting zero when already overdue. Overflow iteration uses that count when no explicit count is supplied, stops when a global interrupt ceiling is reached, and enables throttling after the first iteration.

Software delivery always counts the incoming amount, then requires register context and sampling mode and active state checked under interrupt masking. Period sampling without frequency records the delta as period and forces one overflow; unit sample with unit amount also forces one overflow; otherwise remaining credit is reduced and overflow runs only when credit is exhausted.

Stopped hardware state always excludes delivery. With register context, user mode versus kernel mode is compared against exclusion flags. Software hash acceptance needs matching type and identifier plus non exclusion. Tracepoint acceptance additionally needs non stopped state and a satisfied top level filter.

Bucket selection hashes the combination of type and identifier. One lookup path assumes context lock ownership while another assumes read side protection and may return absent storage. Dispatch walks the selected bucket under read protection and delivers only to entries that match type identifier and exclusion.

Bare software injection needs register context and dispatches under software type with address initialized sample data. Guarded injection disables preemption, obtains recursion protection with silent drop on failure, invokes bare injection, then releases recursion protection and reenables preemption.

Software insertion prepares sampling period state when sampling, sets stopped versus active state from the start request, resolves a bucket with failure when absent, links by RCU and refreshes the user visible page. Removal unlinks by RCU. Start clears stopped state, stop sets it, and read does nothing.

Bucket storage lifetime is serialized by a per CPU mutex with a per CPU reference count. Global acquisition walks all possible CPUs under roster protection and unwinds already acquired CPUs on failure. Release nulls the pointer with deferred freeing. Allocation happens only for online CPUs and reference increment happens even when storage already exists.

Software initialization rejects non software types, branch sampling, clock identifiers with type rewrite, and out of range identifiers. Root events acquire global storage, enable a per identifier static branch, and install a destroy hook. Destroy warns on child events, disables the same static branch, and releases global storage.

Software performance provider targets software task context, declares no NMI support, and binds its own lifecycle operations. Tracepoint provider targets the same context, binds its own initialization and add remove logic, and shares software start stop and read behavior.

Trace submission with attached BPF first exposes registers through raw data and aborts with recursion release when BPF declines or no list remains. Otherwise it forwards count size registers list and task to tracepoint event handling.

Enable count fast path succeeds only while positive and unsaturated. First enabler moves through a transient negative value under mutex to patch code before publishing one. Fast decrement succeeds only above one. Slow decrement warns on negative or zero imbalance and triggers patching when reaching zero.

Slow increment and slow decrement hold CPU read protection across label mutex handling, with decrement asserting that protection is held. Code patching direction observes the enabled view under that serialization.

Patch scope defaults to the core table, moves to module scope when the key resides in a module with coming state controlling init handling, and linked keys iterate per module entry lists skipping empty ones. Entries are visited in order while the key matches and the stop bound is not reached, transforming each eligible entry to the polarity derived from enabled versus branch sense, either directly or through a queued transform flushed at the end with retry after flush when full.
Entries in discarded initialization text are skipped once past initialization, and entries outside kernel text such as built in exit are skipped with a warning unless they are initialization entries.
Count of software static branches equals the maximum software identifier, and per CPU spare register storage has four entries.

Hardware overflow depends on disabled interrupts to exclude concurrent removal from context. Software delivery depends on disabled preemption for object stability plus interrupt masking around the active state check to exclude release progress.
